title: Find and Remove UVM Hotspots with a Profile
description: Measure a slow but correct UVM bench, find five hidden costs (message formatting, configuration lookups, objections, a quadratic search and per-clock coverage sampling) from a profile and operation counters, and remove them without changing what the bench checks.

steps.title: Step 1: Measure the baseline
steps.instructions: Compile lab1_bottleneck/perf_lab_tb.sv once with tb_top as the top module. Run it three times with the same seed, each wrapped in /usr/bin/time -p, and record the median CPU time (user + sys). Record the end time of the run, the SCB_SUMMARY line (matches=1000 mismatches=0 pending=0) and the PERF_SUMMARY counters (fmt=1000 cfg_get=1000 raises=1001 cmp=499500, samples about 4008, cov=100.0) in the README's results table. Never use $time as a speed measurement: it is simulated time.

steps.title: Step 2: Profile and attribute
steps.instructions: Run once with your simulator's profiler on (tool-dependent). Sort by self time and attribute the top rows to DUT, testbench, UVM library and simulator kernel. For each UVM-library row near the top, find its callers and call count. Match each PERF_SUMMARY counter to a profile row and to the line of perf_lab_tb.sv that causes it, and predict which fix will save the most CPU time.

steps.title: Step 3: Remove the five costs, one at a time
steps.instructions: Fix one suspect at a time, recompile, and rerun three times with the same seed. After every change, the end time, SCB_SUMMARY, cov=100.0 and UVM_ERROR : 0 must be identical to the baseline; do not remove any check, message or coverage, and keep creating a new item per packet. Record each run in the results table. The final counters must read fmt=0 cfg_get=1 raises=1 cmp=1000 samples=1000. The README has hints if you are stuck.

steps.title: Step 4 (optional): The analysis FIFO experiment
steps.instructions: Put a uvm_tlm_analysis_fifo between the monitor and the scoreboard and move the checking into a run_phase get() loop, as shown in the README. Predict the counters and the CPU time, then measure. Explain why the CPU time does not drop: what the FIFO's write() does, which process now runs the checks, and whether the simulation runs processes in parallel. Remove the FIFO afterwards.

steps.title: Step 5: Confirm and reflect
steps.instructions: Confirm the final log: PERF_SUMMARY items=1000 fmt=0 cfg_get=1 raises=1 cmp=1000 samples=1000 cov=100.0, SCB_SUMMARY matches=1000 mismatches=0 pending=0, UVM_ERROR : 0, UVM_FATAL : 0, and the same end time as the baseline. Compare your file with solution/perf_lab_tb.sv and answer the four questions in Step 5 of the README.
